 CoRec hosts midterm Election Day voting Tuesday
 The France A. Córdova Recreational Sports Center will host Election Day voting Nov. 3. (Purdue University photo/Alex Kumar) 
 October 29, 2026 
 Purdue Today
 Share
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 Print 
 Polls will be open from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. Tuesday (Nov. 3) for Indiana’s midterm election, and the Córdova Recreational Sports Center (CoRec) will again serve as an Election Day voting site with free transportation provided to the West Lafayette campus community. Indianapolis voting centers will serve registered voters in Marion County at the same time.
 Purdue encourages all eligible individuals to exercise their right to vote. Faculty, staff and students can find more information based on where they are registered:
 Indiana voters 
 Out-of-state voters 
 Additionally, the Office of the Vice Provost for Teaching and Learning website provides more resources, including details for students who plan to vote.
 West Lafayette campus
 Anyone registered to vote in Tippecanoe County may vote at the CoRec, 355 N. Martin Jischke Drive, West Lafayette, or any other voting center in the county during polling hours.
 On-campus faculty, staff and students can get to and from the CoRec using the free Purdue Mall Loop shuttle between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. No preregistration or ride reservations are required, and all Purdue Campus Transit services, routes and times are listed online. Purdue’s Flexigo website and the Flexigo mobile app provide transit vehicle tracking.
 Indianapolis campus 
 For those registered to vote in Marion County, the closest Election Day voting site to Purdue’s Indianapolis campus is Indiana University Indianapolis’ University Library , 755 W. Michigan St., Indianapolis. Parking is available in the nearby North Street Garage, 819 W. North St., and voters will receive a ticket to exit the garage for free.
 Marion County voters may vote at University Library or any other voting center in the county.
 All Indianapolis voting locations and additional information can be found on the IndyVOTES website , and the IndyGo website provides public transportation details.
